title: Wire the coding session
intro: Build the disciplined session the course teaches — two shortcut wires are forbidden.
briefing: Route a task to a commit. The inspector rejects any blueprint where implementation starts without a reviewed plan (plan mode exists for a reason) — or where changes reach the commit without verification (tests or Playwright — nothing lands unverified).

rules.label: The task enters plan mode first
No planless YOLO on a real codebase
The task can actually become a commit

debrief: Task → plan → implement → verify → commit is every lesson of the course in one wire diagram: plan mode before the citation feature, layered tests before the fix, Playwright before the styling sign-off. The two forbidden wires are the two ways agentic coding goes wrong: skipping the plan trades a minute of review for an hour of untangling, and skipping verification is how a confident change becomes a production incident. Note the shape is the SDD pack's workflow at session scale — same discipline, smaller radius, and folio's own PR gate is this blueprint running in CI.
